judgments.title: Spelling error
judgments.reason: “Tule” is unmistakably a typographical error for “rule” in the standard phrase “rule of strict construction.”

judgments.title: Invalid section range in survival provision
judgments.reason: A survival clause may validly include itself, and stating that Sections 4–18 survive does not necessarily state that every omitted section fails to survive. The proposed replacement range is speculative.

judgments.title: Undefined term: Restrictive Covenants
judgments.reason: “Restrictive Covenants” is not expressly defined by reference to particular obligations, creating uncertainty about which breaches qualify as Cause.

judgments.title: Corporation Retains Unilateral Right to Reassign Executive's Role
judgments.reason: The reassignment authority and the Good Reason definition can operate together: a reassignment may be permitted while a materially diminishing reassignment may satisfy Good Reason.

judgments.title: Inconsistent capitalization: client vs Client
judgments.reason: The defined term “Client” is limited to Section 6, while the lowercase use in Section 3 is an ordinary reference to clients and creates no inconsistency.

judgments.title: Corporation Can Reassign Executive's Position Unilaterally
judgments.reason: The Board’s unilateral reassignment authority is clear, and the requested comparability limitation would be a new negotiated protection.

judgments.title: Incorrect section reference in termination provision
judgments.reason: The termination paragraph mechanically refers to Section 4 even though the relevant notice procedure is contained in Section 5.

judgments.title: Second incorrect section reference in termination provision
judgments.reason: The second reference to “this Section 4” is likewise an incorrect internal cross-reference to the termination provision in Section 5.

judgments.title: Grammar error - incorrect preposition
judgments.reason: “In worldwide” is ungrammatical, but the intended meaning—worldwide expansion with a North American focus—is unmistakable.

judgments.title: Annual Bonus Framed as Entitlement Rather Than Discretionary
judgments.reason: The provision clearly creates a conditional contractual right to the bonus; whether Luxoft should prefer discretionary language is a negotiation issue, not a construction defect.

judgments.title: No Clawback Provision for Bonus Payments
judgments.reason: The absence of a clawback right is a missing negotiated protection, not a defect requiring construction.

judgments.title: Annual Bonus Conditioned on Employment on Payment Date
judgments.reason: The payment-date employment condition is explicit. The risk of pre-payment termination is a substantive compensation concern.

pos1.clause_name: Section 4(a) — Base Salary (annual review at Board discretion)
pos1.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: Salary Adjustment at Board's Sole Discretion — No Floor
judgments.reason: The Board’s authority to adjust salary and the Good Reason trigger for a significant reduction can operate together and do not contradict one another.

pos2.clause_name: Section 4(d) — Other Benefits (Stock Option Plan eligibility)
pos2.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: Undefined term: Stock Option Plan
judgments.reason: “Stock Option Plan” is not identified or defined, so the particular plan governing Executive’s eligibility cannot be determined from the agreement.

judgments.title: Stock Option Participation Entirely Discretionary
judgments.reason: Eligibility is expressly subject to Board approval and corporate policies, so the discretionary nature of the benefit is clear.

pos3.clause_name: Section 5(a) — Termination / at-will and ninety days' notice
pos3.label: POSITIVE

judgments.title: 90-Day Notice for Without-Cause Termination Undermines At-Will Status
judgments.reason: The at-will statement is expressly made subject to the contractual 90-day notice right, so the provisions can be harmonized without contradiction.

judgments.title: Invalid section reference in termination provision
judgments.reason: The references to “this Section 4” are incorrect internal cross-references because the termination procedure appears in Section 5.

judgments.title: No Severance Upon Termination Without Cause
judgments.reason: The absence of severance is a substantive compensation choice, not ambiguity, mechanical error, or internal inconsistency.

judgments.title: Corporation Can Accelerate Executive's Departure After Resignation Notice
judgments.reason: The termination clause permits Executive to cease employment activities while preserving a later termination date, while Section 4 conditions compensation on being employed. Read together, the instrument leaves the garden-leave compensation status uncertain.

judgments.title: Lowercase usage of defined term: agreement
judgments.reason: Lowercase “agreement” correctly refers generally to prior agreements in the merger clause, rather than to the defined current “Agreement.”

judgments.title: Typo in section number
judgments.reason: Labeling the section “i4” rather than “14” is a mechanical numbering error that can affect internal navigation and references to Section 14.
